source.paper: arXiv:2602.08316v3, 'SWE Context Bench: A Benchmark for Context Learning in Coding'
source.reproduction_note: This sha256 is byte-identical to the one recorded by the 2026-08-01 retranche log, so the fetch is reproducible. Every cell below was re-parsed from the raw HTML in this lane; none was copied from a prior MemPhant artifact.
source.provenance_class: BENCHMARK AUTHORS' OWN RUNS. Not third-party, not a leaderboard, not vendor-reproduced. No per-instance results are published for any arm, so nothing here can be paired against.

table_3_resolution_on_Related.caption: Performance of five coding agents on SWE-ContextBench under baseline and oracle-summary settings.
table_3_resolution_on_Related.n_note: The paper says 376. The parquet has 376 ROWS over 357 distinct instance_ids; the official Docker registry ships 357 instance tags plus one `base`; the official cases/SWEContextBench Full directory holds 357 case files. 376 = Lite 99 + Verified 166 + Multilingual 111, and Lite INTERSECT Verified = the 19 duplicated ids.

the_number_that_decides_this_lane.what_it_means: 3.72pp is the lift the benchmark's own authors measured for a memory arm that is HANDED the gold parent by construction. It is the ceiling any retrieval-based memory system can approach on this split with this scaffold, and MemPhant's arm can only approach it in proportion to how often it retrieves that parent.

table_4_resolution_on_Related_Lite.caption: Comparison of different context learning settings and memory retrieval frameworks on 99 related tasks from SWE-ContextBench Lite.
table_4_resolution_on_Related_Lite.the_substrate_insight_preregistered_as_s: Memory moves FAIL_TO_PASS tests 19.64 -> 55.95 while moving Resolved only 26.26 -> 30.30, because Patch N/A rises 3.03 -> 10.10 and PASS_TO_PASS falls 94.91 -> 90.23. Memory finds the right code and then breaks the patch. The F2P endpoint carries roughly ten times the effect size of Resolved.
table_4_resolution_on_Related_Lite.power_warning: Every margin here is unmeasurable at n=99. Supermemory's 4.04pp lead over the baseline is a four-instance difference; detecting it has power 0.08-0.15 and needs n = 510-1485. Do not cite this ranking as a measurement, ours or theirs.

table_5_retrieval_quality_on_Related_Lit.caption: Retrieval quality of two context learning settings and four memory retrieval approaches on SWE-ContextBench Lite related tasks.
table_5_retrieval_quality_on_Related_Lit.why_this_table_matters_here: This is the SAME endpoint stage 0 measures -- did the system retrieve the gold parent. The retranche log concluded that no published per-arm results exist and therefore both arms must be ours. That is true for Resolved and FALSE for retrieval: these are published, per-method, on a configuration we can reproduce exactly at $0.
table_5_retrieval_quality_on_Related_Lit.metric: Matched (%) -- the retrieved context is the gold related experience
comparability_caveats_that_must_travel_w: Each method chose its own k. Mem0 and OpenViking report at k=3, LangMem at k=10, Supermemory at k=15. An overall Matched (%) at k=15 is not comparable to one at k=3, and the table does not normalise this. Any MemPhant comparison must state its own k and compare like for like.
n=99. A 10pp difference here is ten instances. These are rankings, not measurements, by this programme's own n_d >= 6 floor.
The pool is the 300-row Lite experience set, not the 1,007-row full pool. Retrieval against 300 candidates is a materially easier problem than against 1,007.
These are the benchmark authors' runs of other people's systems, with no published per-instance detail, so nothing can be paired and no significance test is possible against them.
One gold parent (scikit-learn__scikit-learn-26323) is absent from the 300-row Lite pool, so a strict reproduction has an unreachable edge. It is unknown whether the published numbers account for it.

counts_the_paper_states_versus_counts_me.note: Every measured figure below was counted from the parquets at pinned revision 5bec275a2095768a53ac804ae4fdf90b1723b8af and cross-checked against the official code repo at 31bb04155f52b184bf31b220e3cff0607ac9c953 and against Docker Hub.

related_tasks.explanation: Lite 99 + Verified 166 + Multilingual 111 concatenated; the 19 instances in both Lite and Verified appear twice, with DIFFERENT version / problem_statement / FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS values, and one pair differs in patch, test_patch and base_commit

the_trajectory_pool_is_public.finding: cases/SWEContextBench Lite Past Experience/ contains 300 .jsonl files in the official CODE repo. They are Claude Code session transcripts (type: summary / file-history-snapshot / leafUuid), i.e. the paper's trajectory memory pool, roughly 236 KB and ~117 records each.
the_trajectory_pool_is_public.consequence: The retranche log costed 'rebuild the trajectory pool as the paper does' at ~$737 (1,100 tasks x $0.67). For the Lite universe that rebuild is unnecessary -- the trajectories are already published and free. Only the 707 non-Lite experiences would need generating.
the_trajectory_pool_is_public.caveat: Not verified end to end: the mapping from hash-named .jsonl to instance_id was not established, and the licence position is unchanged (declared-only, no LICENSE file, not redistribution-clear).
